title: You do not know who will benefit you most.
subtitle: Trusting the One who divided it
then: After Uhud, the widow of Sa'd bin Ar-Rabi' came to the Prophet ﷺ with her two daughters. {trap}Their uncle had taken everything their father left.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said Allah would decide, and this verse came. In the old custom only men inherited. {idea}Now every child had a share set by Allah.{/idea} The detailed shares are a science of their own, studied with scholars.
now: Families fight over a house, a car, a few savings. Everyone has a story about who did more, who deserves more, who was the favorite. {trap}It feels like it should be our call.{/trap} The verse says you do not even know whether your parent or your child will be of more benefit to you. {reward}That is why the division belongs to Allah.{/reward}
old: I know best who in my family deserves what.
new: Allah sees what I cannot, so His division is wiser than my favorites.
try: If you are unsure about inheritance in your family, ask a trusted scholar instead of guessing.

title: A will is not a weapon.
subtitle: Last wishes that cause no harm

row.title: settle scores
sub: cut out the one I resent

row.title: without harm
sub: no one wronged by my wishes

then: This verse continues the shares, naming husbands, wives, and brothers and sisters. Woven through it is one condition: {idea}a will made without causing harm.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains this as {trap}not depriving a rightful heir or adding to someone's fixed portion.{/trap} The verse ends by calling Allah Knowing and Forbearing.
now: You hear of someone who changed their will after a family argument. Or who quietly moved everything to one child. {trap}Last words can be used to punish.{/trap} {idea}Your final wishes are one of your last deeds, and Allah sees them.{/idea}
old: What I leave behind is mine to use however I want, even to make a point.
new: My last wishes should leave no one wronged, because they are deeds too.
try: Write down any debts you owe today, even small ones, so they will not be forgotten.

title: A fair final act can crown a whole life.
subtitle: Staying within the limits Allah set

row.title: a fair will
sub: can make the last deed the best

then: After laying out the shares, the verse calls them {idea}the limits of Allah.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said a person may do good for seventy years and then be unjust in his will, or do wrong for years and then be fair in his will, {reward}so his final deed becomes his best.{/reward}
now: You think of your life as the big things: the job, the prayers, the kids raised. But the last decisions matter too. The calls you make when you are old or sick. {reward}It is never too late for a fair act to be the one you are remembered by.{/reward}
old: Only the big parts of my life count. The end is just paperwork.
new: Keeping Allah's limits, even in the paperwork at the end, can be the success that crowns a life.
try: Think of one decision you are putting off that affects others. Make it fair, and make it soon.

title: Overriding Allah's division is disputing His judgment.
subtitle: The other side of the same limits
then: This verse is the mirror of the one before. Ibn Kathir explains that whoever {trap}changes what Allah ordained, by tricks and plots{/trap}, is in effect disputing Allah's judgment. The warning is serious because {idea}the ones harmed are often those too weak to object.{/idea}
now: The sibling who signs papers while the others are not looking. The relative who pressures the grieving widow to sign. {trap}It can all feel like normal family business.{/trap} {idea}Before you push for more than your share, remember who drew the lines.{/idea}
old: Bending the rules a little in family money is normal.
new: When I bend what Allah divided, I am arguing with Him, not with my family.
try: If you have ever taken more than your fair share in a family matter, talk to someone about setting it right.

title: Four witnesses: a very high bar before accusing.
subtitle: Guarding people from careless accusation
then: This verse came early in Madinah, in a society reshaping how it dealt with serious wrongdoing. Ibn Kathir notes it was an early stage, and that {idea}Allah later made another way, as the verse itself promised.{/idea} The verse asks for {reward}four witnesses{/reward} before anything happens. The rulings themselves are for scholars and courts, not for individuals.
now: A screenshot is passed around. Someone says they heard something about a woman at the mosque. {trap}It takes one message to ruin a name.{/trap} The verse sets the bar so high that {idea}rumor counts for nothing.{/idea} That is your cue to stay silent too.
old: If many people are saying it, it is probably true.
new: Without clear proof, I have no right to repeat it.
try: The next time a rumor about someone reaches you, do not forward it. Delete it.

title: If they turned back, stop reminding them.
subtitle: Letting go after real repentance

row.title: turn away from it
sub: as if there was no sin

then: Like the verse before, this was an early stage that later rulings replaced, and those details belong to scholars. What stays is the ending: {idea}if they repent and correct themselves, leave them alone.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says {reward}do not abuse them with words after that, since one who truly repents is like one who has no sin.{/reward}
now: A cousin who once went off the rails is now praying again. A friend who wronged you has changed. But at every family dinner, someone brings up the old story. {trap}The past gets used as a leash.{/trap} {reward}If Allah is Accepting of repentance, who are you to keep the file open?{/reward}
old: People who did something bad should never live it down.
new: If Allah accepts someone's repentance, I should stop holding their past over them.
try: Think of someone whose old mistake you still mention. Decide not to bring it up again.

title: Every sin is done in a moment of not knowing better.
subtitle: The door Allah keeps open to those who return soon

row.title: a wrong done
sub: in ignorance, in a weak moment

row.title: too late for me
sub: I knew what I was doing

then: The Companions used to say that {idea}every sin is committed out of ignorance{/idea}, even a deliberate one. And "soon" was explained generously: Ikrimah said {reward}all of this life is soon.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said Allah accepts a servant's repentance until the soul reaches the throat.
now: You did something last night you said you would never do again. Now the shame says: you knew better, there is no point. {trap}That voice sounds humble, but it shuts the door.{/trap} {reward}The verse opens it. Turn back today.{/reward}
old: I knew it was wrong and did it anyway, so I cannot be forgiven.
new: Every sin is a lapse of knowing better, and Allah accepts those who return while they still can.
try: Before you sleep tonight, sincerely ask Allah's forgiveness for one specific thing.

title: Saying I repent now, at the very last moment.
subtitle: Why the door should not be left to the end
then: The previous verse opened the door wide. This one shows where it closes. Ibn Kathir explains that once {trap}death is actually present and the soul is being drawn out{/trap}, the chance to repent has passed. The verse speaks of those who kept going until that moment. {idea}The lesson is to turn back while there is time.{/idea}
now: You tell yourself you will sort it out when you are older, after the wedding, after this job. {trap}None of us is promised the next decade, or the next week.{/trap} {idea}The best day to come back is the one you are in.{/idea}
old: I have plenty of time to change before the end.
new: I do not know when my time ends, so the right time to turn back is now.
try: Pick one habit you have been planning to quit someday. Take the first step today.

title: Maybe what you dislike holds much good.
subtitle: Living with kindness, even through dislike

row.title: inheritance
sub: his male relatives decide for her

key.label: When you dislike something in them

row.title: much good
sub: you may not see it yet

then: Ibn Abbas described a custom: when a man died, {trap}his male relatives could do what they wished with his widow{/trap}, as if she were part of his estate. This verse ended that and said: {idea}live with them in kindness.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said the best of you is the best to his family, and he would race with A'ishah and laugh with his wives.
now: You are irritated with your spouse again. The same habit, the same argument. {trap}Your mind starts keeping a list of everything wrong.{/trap} The verse says: maybe the thing you dislike is where Allah has placed a lot of good. {reward}If one trait annoys you, another one you love is right beside it.{/reward}
old: If something about them bothers me, I am allowed to be cold about it.
new: Kindness is my part even when I dislike something, and Allah may put good right there.
try: Tell someone at home one thing you appreciate about them today, out loud.

title: Even a heap of gold, once given, stays given.
subtitle: Not taking back gifts when love ends
then: The verse imagines a man moving on to another marriage who wants back what he gave his first wife. {trap}Would you take it unjustly, as a plain sin?{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes the verse shows a gift could be very large, and that Umar later changed his view about limiting it. {idea}What was given stays hers.{/idea}
now: A relationship ends badly. Suddenly there is a list: the ring, the phone, the money I spent on you. {trap}Hurt makes you want to take everything back.{/trap} {idea}A gift does not become a loan just because love faded.{/idea}
old: If it ended, I have the right to get back what I gave.
new: What I gave with an open hand stays given, even when things end.
try: Let go of one thing you once gave someone and still secretly want back.
